'''Julie Anne Genter''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|MP|size=85%}} ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|dʒ|ɛ|n|t|ər}}; born 17 December 1979) is an American-born New Zealand politician. She has served as a [[Member of parliament#New Zealand|Member of Parliament]] for the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand]] since 2011, first as a [[Electoral list|list]] member, and since 2023, for the [[Rongotai (New Zealand electorate)|Rongotai]] electorate. She served as the [[Minister for Women (New Zealand)|Minister for Women]], Associate Minister for Health and Associate Minister for Transport during the first term of the [[Sixth Labour Government of New Zealand|Sixth Labour Government]].<ref name="Stuff Mother to be" /> She holds [[dual citizenship]] of New Zealand and the United States.<ref>{{cite web|title=Genter, Julie-Anne|url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/50HansS_20140527_00000917/genter-julie-anne-taxation-annual-rates-employee-allowances |website=Hansard Reports|publisher=New Zealand Parliament|date=27 May 2014}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Genter was born in [[Rochester, Minnesota]], United States, in 1979, and grew up in [[Los Angeles]], California.<ref>{{cite news |url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10763970 |title= Greens buoyed by prospect of having 15 MPs | work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date= 5 November 2011 |access-date= 15 February 2012}}</ref> She gained a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in philosophy from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 2003.<ref name="JAG CV">{{cite web|last=Genter|first=Julie Anne|title=Julie Anne Genter|url= http://www.julieanne.co.nz/files/CV-Julie-Anne-Genter.pdf |publisher= www.julieanne.co.nz |access-date=30 November 2011 |year=2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201154532/http://www.julieanne.co.nz/files/CV-Julie-Anne-Genter.pdf |archive-date=1 February 2014}}</ref> She moved to France where in 2005 she obtained a post-graduate certificate in International Political Studies from the [[Sciences Po|Institut d'études politiques]] in Paris.<ref name="JAG CV" /> She gained a Masters of Planning Practice from the [[University of Auckland]] in 2008.<ref name="About me">{{cite web|title=Julie Anne Genter|url=http://julieanne.co.nz/about-julie-anne.html|publisher=julieanne.co.nz|access-date=30 November 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111120191039/http://www.julieanne.co.nz/about-julie-anne.html|archive-date=20 November 2011}}</ref>

==Professional life==
Genter has worked as a transportation planner since coming to New Zealand in 2006. She was first employed by [[Sinclair Knight Merz]], then by MRCagney (formerly McCormick Rankin Cagney) from 2008.<ref name="JAG CV" />

She has advised numerous councils in Australasia on transportation,<ref name="Saturday Morning" /> and appeared on [[TV One (New Zealand)|TVNZ]]'s ''[[Breakfast (TVNZ programme)|Breakfast]]'' programme<ref>{{cite web|title=Julie Anne on TVNZ's Breakfast|url=http://julieanne.co.nz/media.html|publisher=julieanne.co.nz|access-date=30 November 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222080000/http://julieanne.co.nz/media.html|archive-date=22 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Breakfast: Wednesday December 9|url= http://tvnz.co.nz/breakfast-news/breakfast-wednesday-december-9-3242419 | work=TVNZ |access-date=30 November 2011 |date=9 December 2009}}</ref> and [[Kim Hill (broadcaster)|Kim Hill]]'s ''Saturday Morning'' programme on [[Radio New Zealand National]].<ref name="Saturday Morning">{{cite news|title=Saturday Morning|url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/national/programmes/saturday/20101113 |access-date=30 November 2011 |work=Radio New Zealand National |date=13 November 2010}}</ref>

===In opposition, 2011–2017===
Placed in 13th place on the Green Party list for the {{NZ election link|2011}},<ref name="Green Party list">{{cite web |title=2011 election candidates |url=http://www.greens.org.nz/people/candidates |publisher=Green Party |access-date=26 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130212134844/http://www.greens.org.nz/people/candidates |archive-date=12 February 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Genter entered Parliament, with the Greens gaining 14 List Members of Parliament.<ref name="2011 election night commentary">{{cite news|last=Trevett|first=Claire|title=National soars as Labour put to the sword|url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=10769072 |access-date=26 November 2011 | work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=27 November 2011}}</ref><ref name="25 new MPs">{{cite news|title=Big batch of new MPs for Parliament |url= http://tvnz.co.nz/national-news/big-batch-new-mps-parliament-4576904 |access-date=30 November 2011|work=TVNZ|date=28 November 2011}}</ref>

In July 2015 Genter became the third ever female MP to hold a finance portfolio, alongside the Transport and Youth portfolios.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/70175855/greens-portfolio-reshuffle-sees-thirdever-woman-finance-spokesperson|title=Greens: Portfolio reshuffle sees third-ever woman finance spokesperson|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=12 July 2015 |access-date=10 February 2017}}</ref> The departure of long-standing Health Spokesperson [[Kevin Hague]] in September 2016 led to her taking on the Health portfolio, keeping Transport, Youth, Auckland Issues, and Associate Finance.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/84784353/greens-reshuffle-their-lineup-new-mp-and-new-finance-and-health-spokespeople|title=Greens reshuffle their lineup: New MP and new finance and health spokespeople|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=28 September 2016 |access-date=10 February 2017}}</ref>

As an MP, Genter criticised the [[Fifth National Government of New Zealand|Fifth National government]] for spending billions of dollars on motorways,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/JulieAnneGenter/videos/1396262643719376/|title=When the National Govt tries to claim... – Julie Anne Genter MP {{!}} Facebook|website=[[Facebook]]|language=en|access-date=10 February 2017}}</ref> called for a nationwide mental health inquiry,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.greens.org.nz/news/press-release/mental-health-system-crying-out-help|title=Mental health system crying out for help|date=27 January 2017|work=Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|access-date=10 February 2017|language=en}}</ref> and questioned Health Minister [[Jonathan Coleman (politician)|Jonathan Coleman]] on his use of a [[Coca-Cola]] funded study.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/health/87353490/green-party-criticises-health-ministers-stance-on-sugary-drinks-tax|title=Green Party criticises health minister's stance on sugary drinks tax|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=8 December 2016 |access-date=10 February 2017}}</ref> In January 2017 Genter criticised former Green Party issues director [[Laila Harré]], stating that the reason Harré gave for resigning from the Greens was not factual. Genter quickly apologised to Harré stating "regret any slight to your integrity".<ref>{{Cite news| url = http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11789854| title = Green MP Julie Ann Genter apologises for criticising Laila Harre, regrets slighting her integrity| work = [[The New Zealand Herald]]| access-date = 27 January 2017| date = 27 January 2017}}</ref>

In late 2016 Genter announced that she would be putting her name forward for the Green Party nomination for the [[2017 Mount Albert by-election|Mount Albert by-election]],<ref name="green">{{Cite news |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11772229|title=Green Party to contest Mt Albert byelection against Labour candidate Jacinda Ardern| work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|author=Nicholas Jones|date=23 December 2016|access-date=23 December 2016}}</ref><ref name="greens">{{Cite press release |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1612/S00268/green-party-decision-on-mt-albert-by-election.htm |title=Green Party decision on Mt Albert by-election | agency=[[Scoop (website)]] | publisher=[[New Zealand Labour Party]] |date=23 December 2016 |access-date=23 December 2016}}</ref><ref name="mt albert greens">{{Cite news |url=https://i.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/87898480/green-party-to-stand-against-labour-in-mt-albert-byelection |title=Green Party to stand against Labour in Mt Albert by-election| work=[[stuff.co.nz]]|date=23 December 2016 |access-date=23 December 2016}}</ref> which she gained in January.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11781265 |title=Mt Albert byelection: It's Jacinda Ardern v Julie Anne Genter | work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] | first=Nicholas | last=Jones |date=12 January 2017 |access-date=12 January 2017}}</ref> Genter came second in the February 2017 by-election after [[Jacinda Ardern]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mt Albert – Official Result |url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/2017_mt_albert_byelection/ |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=11 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812145321/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2017_mt_albert_byelection/ |archive-date=12 August 2020 |date=12 August 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Genter stated that she rebuffed an approach by [[Gareth Morgan (economist)|Gareth Morgan]] to [[Waka-jumping|waka-jump]] to his [[The Opportunities Party]] (TOP) in July 2017, though TOP denied any "formal" approach had been made.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/94508451/senior-green-mp-says-she-rebuffed-top-party-call-for-her-to-jump-ship |title=Senior Green MP says she rebuffed TOP party call for her to jump ship | work=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |author-link=Vernon Small | first=Vernon | last=Small |date=7 July 2017 |access-date=5 September 2017}}</ref> At the {{NZ election link|2017}}, Genter was re-elected to parliament on the Green Party list.<ref>{{cite web|title=2017 General Election – Official Result Successful Candidates|url=http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/successful-candidates.html|publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]|access-date=26 October 2017}}</ref>

===In Government, 2017–2023===
When the Labour Party and the Green Party formed [[Sixth Labour Government of New Zealand|a new government with New Zealand First]], Genter was appointed [[Minister for Women (New Zealand)|Minister for Women]] and Associate Minister of both Health and Transport.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ministerial List |url=https://www.dpmc.govt.nz/our-business-units/cabinet-office/ministers-and-their-portfolios/ministerial-list |publisher=[[Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (New Zealand)|Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet]]|access-date=26 October 2017}}</ref><ref name="Stuff Mother to be">{{cite news |last1=Mann |first1=Britt |title=Julie Anne Genter: Minister for Women, mother-to-be, full-time feminist |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/101725307/julie-anne-genter-minister-for-women-mothertobe-fulltime-feminist |access-date=11 November 2020 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=4 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109023959/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/101725307/julie-anne-genter-minister-for-women-mothertobe-fulltime-feminist |archive-date=9 November 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Genter chose to take her oath to the Crown in [[Te Reo Māori]] along with other members, for which she was praised by political colleagues and members of the public.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Roy|first1=Eleanor Ainge|title=Jacinda Ardern sworn in as New Zealand PM, promising 'empathetic' government|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/oct/26/jacinda-ardern-sworn-in-new-zealand-pm-empathetic-government|website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=3 February 2018|language=en|date=26 October 2017}}</ref>

In 2018 Genter added Civil Aviation to her portfolio as Associate Minister of Transport, after Transport Minister [[Phil Twyford]] was reported for making a phone call from an airplane preparing for departure.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Watkins|first1=Tracy|last2=Moir|first2=Jo|title=Minister Phil Twyford apologises for Civil Aviation breach|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/104196693/minister-phil-twyford-apologises-for-civil-aviation-breach|access-date=24 May 2018| work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]|date=24 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190213222152/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/104196693/minister-phil-twyford-apologies-for-civil-aviation-breach|archive-date=13 February 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Bennett|first1=Lucy|title=Grounded: Phil Twyford offers to resign, stripped of role after phone call on plane|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12058025|access-date=24 May 2018| work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=24 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109043613/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/grounded-phil-twyford-offers-to-resign-stripped-of-role-after-phone-call-on-plane/7GVV2557BPC4UHSV52SBDFSGBE/|archive-date=9 November 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>
[[File:JAG UC Greens 2.jpg|thumb|Genter with [[University of Canterbury]] Greens]]
Genter was re-elected to Parliament on the Green party list in the October [[2020 New Zealand election]],<ref>{{cite web|title=2020 General Election and Referendums – Official Result Successful Candidates|url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/successful-candidates.html|publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]|access-date=11 November 2020|archive-date=7 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201107204759/https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/successful-candidates.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> when the Greens earned 7.9% of the popular vote.<ref>{{cite web |title=2020 General Election and Referendums – Official Result |url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230621001306/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=21 June 2023 |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=11 November 2020 }}</ref> [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour]] formed a majority government, and invited only the co-leaders of the Green Party to join Cabinet.<ref>{{cite news|last=Roy|first=Eleanor Ainge|date=31 October 2020|title=New Zealand Greens accept Ardern's offer of 'cooperation agreement'|language=en-GB|work=The Observer|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/31/new-zealand-greens-accept-arderns-offer-of-cooperation-agreement|access-date=1 November 2020|issn=0029-7712|archive-date=1 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101010850/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/31/new-zealand-greens-accept-arderns-offer-of-cooperation-agreement|url-status=live}}</ref> Genter therefore stood down from her ministerial portfolios, but was granted retention of the title "[[The Honourable]]" for life in recognition of her term as a member of the [[Executive Council of New Zealand|Executive Council]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://gazette.govt.nz/notice/id/2020-vr5185 |title=Retention of the title "The Honourable" |date=10 November 2020 |work=[[New Zealand Gazette]] |access-date=10 November 2020}}</ref>

Genter was named Green Party spokesperson for Building and Construction, COVID-19 Response, Customs, Energy and Resources, Finance, Infrastructure, Local Government, State Owned Enterprises, Transport, and Urban Development.<ref>{{cite web |title=Green Party Announce Portfolio Reshuffle With Talented And Energised Caucus Team |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2011/S00072/green-party-announce-portfolio-reshuffle-with-talented-and-energised-caucus-team.htm |website=Scoop |publisher=Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand |access-date=23 November 2020}}</ref>

===In opposition, 2023–present===
At the [[2023 New Zealand general election|2023 general election]], Genter stood as a 'two-tick' candidate, seeking both the party vote and electorate vote.<ref>{{cite news |last1=MacManus |first1=Joel |title=For the first time ever, Rongotai is interesting |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/04-09-2023/for-the-first-time-ever-rongotai-is-interesting |access-date=15 May 2024 |work=[[The Spinoff]] |date=4 September 2023 |language=en}}</ref> The campaign was successful, with the [[Rongotai (New Zealand electorate)|Rongotai electorate]] choosing a non-Labour representative for the first time ever.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023 General Election: Successful candidates |url=https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/successful-candidates.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=20 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231117114239/https://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/successful-candidates.html |archive-date=17 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> Genter received 2,717 more votes than Labour's candidate, [[Fleur Fitzsimons]] and almost twice as many votes as the third-placed National Party candidate.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rongotai – Official Result |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-43.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=15 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231125010112/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/electorate-details-43.html |archive-date=25 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 29 November 2023, Genter assumed the Green Party's transport, infrastructure, urban development, building and construction, economic development, and state owned enterprises spokesperson portfolios.<ref>{{cite news |title=Greens unveil portfolio spokespeople |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2023/11/29/greens-unveil-portfolio-spokespeople/ |access-date=23 February 2024 |work=[[1News]] |date=29 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128214920/https://www.1news.co.nz/2023/11/29/greens-unveil-portfolio-spokespeople/ |archive-date=28 November 2023}}</ref>

On 1 May 2024 during a parliamentary debate on roading projects, Genter walked over to  from her seat and yelled "Read the report!" at National MP and Minister [[Matt Doocey]]. Genter returned to her seat then rose and apologised. The Speaker later said he would refer Genter to Parliament's privileges committee.<ref name="1News">{{cite news |last1=Sherman |first1=Maiki |title=Julie Anne Genter breaks silence - and offers three more apologies |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/05/07/julie-anne-genter-breaks-silence-and-offers-three-more-apologies/ |access-date=7 May 2024 |work=[[1News]] |date=7 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240507081827/https://www.1news.co.nz/2024/05/07/julie-anne-genter-breaks-silence-and-offers-three-more-apologies/|archive-date=7 May 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> In the following days, two Wellington small business owners publicised their own complaints about arguments they had had with Genter over her advocacy of cycleways in the city,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=Jenna |title='She's a bully': Newshub reveals new allegation of intimidation against Green MP |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/05/julie-anne-genter-outburst-fresh-allegation-of-intimidation-surfaces-against-green-mp.html|access-date=2 May 2024 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=1 May 2024 |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240502212549/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2024/05/julie-anne-genter-outburst-fresh-allegation-of-intimidation-surfaces-against-green-mp.html|archive-date=2 May 2024|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Georgina |title=Wellington business owner Nicola Cranfield claims Green MP Julie Anne Genter grabbed her |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/wellington-business-owner-nicola-cranfield-claims-green-mp-julie-anne-genter-grabbed-her/JDNK2H7VHBA4HLMLPPT2CCJQTY/ |access-date=4 May 2024 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=4 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240504105212/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/wellington-business-owner-nicola-cranfield-claims-green-mp-julie-anne-genter-grabbed-her/JDNK2H7VHBA4HLMLPPT2CCJQTY/|archive-date=4 May 2024|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="The Post grabbed">{{cite news |last1=Whyte |first1=Anna |title=Business owner alleges she was 'grabbed' by Julie Anne Genter |url=https://www.thepost.co.nz/politics/350267356/business-owner-alleges-she-was-grabbed-julie-anne-genter |access-date=6 May 2024 |work=[[The Post (New Zealand)|The Post]] |date=4 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240506025146/https://www.thepost.co.nz/politics/350267356/business-owner-alleges-she-was-grabbed-julie-anne-genter |archive-date=6 May 2024|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and a City Councillor alleged a similar incident from five years earlier.<ref name="The Post grabbed"/> Genter apologised for her exchanges with the business owners.<ref name="1News"/>

On 1 August 2024, Genter was found in contempt of Parliament, censured and ordered to apologise after shouting at Doocey in May 2024. The Green Party described her actions as unacceptable and in breach of standards expected of MPs.<ref>{{cite news |title=Julie Anne Genter to be censured and apologise over shouting incident |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/523846/julie-anne-genter-to-be-censured-and-apologise-over-shouting-incident |access-date=1 August 2024 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=1 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240801002603/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/523846/julie-anne-genter-to-be-censured-and-apologise-over-shouting-incident |archive-date=1 August 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On 18 February 2018, Genter announced that she was pregnant,<ref>{{cite web|title=Greens MP Julie Anne Genter pregnant – baby due in August |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11997062 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=18 February 2018 |date=18 February 2018 }}</ref> having previously revealed that she had suffered a series of miscarriages.<ref>{{cite news |title=Green MP reveals miscarriage |url=http://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2017/03/green-mp-reveals-miscarriage.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180218090631/http://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2017/03/green-mp-reveals-miscarriage.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 February 2018 |website=[[Newshub]] |access-date=18 February 2018 |date=13 March 2017 }}</ref> In August, Genter gave birth to a baby boy, announcing the news on her social media.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/life-style/parenting/baby/106401717/green-party-mp-julie-anne-genter-becomes-a-mum-for-first-time |title=Green Party MP Julie Anne Genter becomes a mum for first time |date=22 August 2018 |work=Stuff.co.nz}}</ref> She made international headlines after she and her partner cycled to [[Auckland Hospital]] for her labour to be [[Labor induction|induced]].<ref name="nyt">{{cite news |last1=Graham-McLay |first1=Charlotte |title=Pregnant Minister Cycles to Hospital to Give Birth |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/08/19/world/asia/new-zealand-pregnant-minister-bicycle.html |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=The New York Times |date=19 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/lifestyle/news/article.cfm?c_id=6&objectid=12109995 |title=Pregnant Julie Anne Genter's cycle to hospital makes world-wide headlines |date=20 August 2018 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] }}</ref><ref name=preg2>{{cite news |last1=Lang |first1=Sarah |title=Julie Anne Genter's baby joy: 'I've never been so emotional' |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/lifestyle/green-mp-julie-anne-genter-reveals-why-her-second-pregnancy-is-different-never-been-so-emotional/QNGTGSCG3JRNWU3ZUKRHWY7WQE/ |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}}</ref>

In early 2019, Genter and her partner Peter Nunns moved to live in [[Wellington]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nowtolove.co.nz/parenting/family/julie-anne-genter-adjusting-to-motherhood-has-been-roller-coaster-minister-for-women-44642|title=Minister for Women Julie Anne Genter says adjusting to motherhood has been a roller coaster|first=Karyn|last=Henger|publisher=Now To Love|date=6 March 2020}}</ref> In November 2021, she once again cycled to hospital to give birth to her second child, a daughter.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/456729/julie-anne-genter-cycles-to-hospital-to-give-birth |title=Julie Anne Genter cycles to hospital to give birth |date=28 November 2021 |publisher=[[RNZ]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/127121005/green-mp-julie-anne-genter-cycles-to-hospital-while-in-labour--again |title=Green MP Julie Anne Genter cycles to hospital while in labour – again |date=28 November 2021 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |first=Brittney |last=Deguara}}</ref>

==Views and positions==
===Women===
In her three years as Minister for Women, Genter worked to reduce the public-sector gender pay gap, and increased funding for primary maternity services.<ref name=preg2/>

===Transport incentives and funding===
Genter and the Green Party support a "feebate" scheme introduced by the [[Sixth Labour Government of New Zealand#Second term (2020–present)|Labour-led]] government to encourage a shift from petrol vehicles with high emissions of polluting material to electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/06/prime-minister-jacinda-ardern-considered-exemption-for-utes-in-electric-car-incentive-scheme-but-ruled-it-out.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210616081746/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2021/06/prime-minister-jacinda-ardern-considered-exemption-for-utes-in-electric-car-incentive-scheme-but-ruled-it-out.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 June 2021|title=Jacinda Ardern considered exemption for utes in electric car incentive scheme but ruled it out|newspaper=[[Newshub]] |date=16 June 2021}}</ref>  When serving as Associate Minister of Transport in the previous term of government, Genter had been involved in the development of a similar policy which was blocked by [[New Zealand First]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Coughlan |first1=Thomas |title=NZ First axes Government's 'feebate' electric vehicle subsidy plan, while Greens vow to take the policy to the election |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/119713361/nz-first-axe-governments-electric-vehicle-subsidy-plan-while-greens-vow-to-take-the-policy-to-the-election |access-date=26 June 2021 |publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=21 February 2020}}</ref> The scheme saw the sale of high-emitting vehicles being subject to a fee of up to $5,000 to fund rebates for electric and [[plug-in hybrid]] vehicles. Genter said on Twitter that the Ford Ranger was advertised as "all about lifestyle and status for men who want to feel more masculine," in the context of debate as to whether such vehicles were used for work purposes or as "a fashion choice for city dwellers." Genter later acknowledged that Ford Rangers are used for work by some, and said: "I was tweeting about how they are marketed, not a statement about everyone using one."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/pm-defends-feebates-move-as-the-work-ute-vs-remuera-tractor-debate-sparks-up/ANHVKBFGPWY3E3PM7L4LFRPDFI/|title=PM defends 'feebates' move as the work ute vs Remuera tractor debate sparks up|publisher=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=14 June 2021}}</ref>

Genter negotiated for the Government to remove fringe benefit tax on employer payments for public transport, to match the tax exemption for work-provided carparks,<ref>{{cite web |title='Tax legislation makes Green Party change to public transport tax rules' |url=http://www.voxy.co.nz/politics/5/406570 |website=www.voxy.co.nz |publisher=Digital Advance Limited |access-date=14 October 2022 |language=en}}</ref> and introduced subsidies for [[Electric bicycle|e-bikes]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Government employees to get e-bike discount of up to 50 percent |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/405461/government-employees-to-get-e-bike-discount-of-up-to-50-percent |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=13 December 2019 |language=en-nz}}</ref>

Genter has been a strong supporter of better passenger rail between Auckland, Hamilton and Tauranga.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jones |first1=Nicolas |title=Auckland-Hamilton-Tauranga rail plan |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/green-party-promises-auckland-hamilton-tauranga-passenger-rail/FTDCHY5BVDDTYLYO2KZQNN3QH4/ |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}}</ref> As chair of the government's Infrastructure Committee, she promoted further investment in regional passenger rail services.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Galuszka |first1=Jono |title=Politicians keen to hear people's thoughts on rail services between regions |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/300660825/politicians-keen-to-hear-peoples-thoughts-on-rail-services-between-regions |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=12 August 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
:
During the [[COVID-19]] lockdown of 2020, Genter increased funding for [[tactical urbanism]], enabling rapid expansion of cycle lanes and footpaths.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Reid |first1=Carlton |title=New Zealand First Country To Fund Pop-Up Bike Lanes, Widened Sidewalks During Lockdown |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/carltonreid/2020/04/13/new-zealand-first-country-to-fund-pop-up-bike-lanes-widened-sidewalks-during-lockdown/?sh=b7a29c2546e1 |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=Forbes |date=13 April 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

===Transport safety===
As Associate Minister for Transport, Genter introduced lower speed limits around all schools, supported by funding for signs and speed cameras.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hutt |first1=Kendall |title=Government to lower speed limits around schools, add more speed cameras |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/education/117772084/government-to-lower-speed-limits-around-schools |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=28 November 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

===Health===
As Associate Minister for Health, Genter introduced government funding for spouses, partners and parents who care for a family member with disabilities.<ref>{{cite news |title=Family carers to be paid fairer wage |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/393821/family-carers-to-be-paid-fairer-wage |access-date=14 October 2022 |work=[[RNZ]] |date=7 July 2019 |language=en-nz}}</ref>

===Abortion===
Genter voted in favour of legislation that decriminalises [[abortions|abortion]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/114855678/abortion-law-reform-passes-first-reading-clearing-a-major-hurdle|title=Abortion law passes first hurdle 94 votes to 23|publisher=[[Newshub]] |date=8 August 2019}}</ref>

===Cannabis===
Genter supports legalising while also regulating the use of [[cannabis]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/94358954/julie-anne-genter-and-simon-oconnor-debate-cannabis-reform|title=Julie Anne Genter and Simon O'Connor debate cannabis reform|publisher=Stuff NZ|date=5 July 2017}}</ref>
